what: route-impact verification of the v5 STOP (in-sample screen) before recording E; extra to the pinned freeze audit (not a §B11.2 audit)
agents: 3 independent checkers (independent recomputation of P2, P3-1, P4-1, P5a-1, P7a-1; screen() vs text for all failed rows; route-impact sweep of the 39 findings + 6 gaps) + 1 judge
decisive_reasons: No screen-only fix can turn this STOP into a PASS. v5 §B5 (docs/plans/day_pattern_metanet_protocol_v5.md:368) says: 'If any screened row fails, the route STOPs at the freeze'. The committed record docs/lab/day_pattern/metanet_v5_calibration.json has route 'STOP (in-sample screen)', and I checked that its stop_detail screen is byte-identical (as sorted JSON) to freeze_stops.json detail['in-sample screen'] (code 3d4402fd). 12 screened rows fail. Reversal needs all 12 to pass, and several fail on point statistics that no disputed item touches: P7b share 3/22 = 0.136 against '>= 70 %' (vsl_lab/jobs/metanet_gate.py:399-400); P7a-1 median 62.5 min against 'median <= 30 min' (gate.py:375); P7c 55 min against <= 30 (gate.py:401-402); P1c median_D_N2 = +0.198 against 'vs N2: median paired difference < 0' (v3:895; gate.py:297, a point median with no CI); P6-1 with R = 11/11, M = 9/8, k_h = 2. P6-1 needs >= 18 model-active days, and the model has 17, so no demand split can pass it.

Every real-data minimum is met, so no row can move to 'reported, not screened'. The minima are v3 §5.2 (v3:849-852): n_val >= 16, n_A,k >= 8, n_H,k >= 6, n_H,first >= 6. The recorded counts are n = 22, n_A 22/9, n_H 22/9 and n_H,first 22, with reported_not_screened = []. v5:363 reads 'A row whose real-data minimum (§5.2) is not met ... is reported, not screened', and that does not apply here. v3:880 has one reading: 'When the real minima are met, a model-dependent shortfall is a FAIL ... never INCONCLUSIVE'. So the count failures stand: P5a-1 and P5b-1 (15 < 17), P9 (15 < 17) and P5c (4 < 7).

The only way to reverse the STOP is a fix on the calibration/J5 path that moves the nominal, because §B11.2 item 1 re-runs 'CMA-ES, the freeze stops, the screen ...' on the original seeds. No one-reading deviation was found on that path. s1_ratio is called only at gate.py:446 (P9), and no J5 module uses it (grep). J5's P5c day set is both_q, exactly as v5:127 says ('the gate's `both_q`'). j5-04 concerns only a missing count; the items are still 'left out of its row mean' (v5:164). j5-05 acts only inside sensitivities(), which never ran. According to report 3, loo_nulls equals G.nulls on the other 21 days, bit for bit, on all 22 days.

The candidate items on the J5 path admit more than one reading, so the code's reading stands. v5 §B11.2 item 1 (v5:539): 'Where the text admits more than one reading, the reading of the code that passed the pre-launch code-review checkpoint (§B8 step 3) stands, before and after any result ... It is never "fixed" after a result'. The items are:
- A1: c = 1 at S453. v3:518 computes c_s only for 'every interior station and for T.H.101', and v3:241 calls S453 the 'upstream boundary (input only)'. The text gives no c_s for S453; the code discloses this at metanet_postcal.py:100-101.
- A2: the merge gap. The code counts empty bins, s - prev_end - 1 < 6, which is the natural reading of 'separated by < 30 min'.
- A4: the t_c window end.
- A3: the tie order.
According to report 1, the A3 and A4 alternatives change nothing on the 22 calibration days.

The headline numbers were reproduced independently. Report 1 used its own implementation and rebuilt the real event layer from raw calibration-day Mayfly data, which matched the committed facts. It got P2 16/22, P3-1 16/22, P4-1 17/26 with a 20-min median, P5a-1 15/17 with median D -0.0561, and P7a-1 62.5 min, all equal to the record. Report 2 re-ran screen() at HEAD and got every row identical to 1e-12. No alternative reading the checkers tested flips any row: overlap ±55/±65 min, match window ±95 min, the merge-gap alternative (P7a-1 goes to 67.5, which is worse), unmasked model flow, and the t_c window at e+7.

regression-01: vsl_lab/jobs/metanet_items.py:96-101, s1_ratio. For a 1-2-bin window it returns seg.sum()/3 (verified), against v3 §5.4 'the maximum 3-bin rolling 15-min flow ... in [onset − 60 min, end]'. Latent; not exercised on the calibration days; reaches P9 only. Two notes for the fix record:
- The replacement value is itself a reading choice. Returning None matches the code's own 'valid' convention and its empty-window rule (docstring at :94-95).
- A synthetic 1-bin test fails before the fix.

Critic gap 2: the §B11.2 item 4 labels ('second look on the same validation days', 'after post-result fix') are not implemented in verdict() or finalize(). They act only after a fix or on the gate path.

Procedural consequence for all of the above: §B11.2 item 1 requires each fix to be followed by 'calibration and the gate ... re-run in full on the original seeds'. None of these fixes touches J5, so the re-run should reproduce nominal 7192011 and the same STOP if the pipeline is deterministic. That determinism was not re-checked: not determined.
disagreements_resolved: P4-1 CI resampling unit. Report 1 calls it not one-reading; reports 2 and 3 are silent. v3:1006 says 'percentile bootstrap over days for medians'. The code resamples the 26 per-episode values instead (gate.py:332, boot_median_ci(dts)). Judge: the literal reading would be a day-cluster bootstrap, but 'over days' can fairly be read as a general convention written for the per-day rows, so I treat it as contested. Either way the CI is report-only: the P4 criterion is 'median <= 15 min and >= 75 % of them matched' (v3:898; gate.py:333). Not route-changing. Disclose it as an ambiguity. - v3:884 '>= max(6, ⌈0.75 · n_H,both⌉)'.

Report 1 found 'no one-reading deviation' while reports 2 and 3 list several. This is not a conflict: report 1 was scoped to five rows (P2, P3-1, P4-1, P5a-1, P7a-1), and the deviations the others found lie in P5c, P9, report-only output, the record, the grid/gate stages or the tests.

P9 truncation count. Report 3 gives 6 truncated days, against truncated = 3 in the record. Both are right: report 3 counts over all 22 real heavy-first days, while the code counts only the 15 matched days (gate.py:433-441), and 0607, 0621 and 1115 are among the unmatched days.

P5a matching. Report 1 tested matching the 'longest real alone'; report 2 describes the matched partner of the longest episode. No conflict: the code matches all real episodes one-to-one and takes the partner of the longest (metanet_postcal.py:246-251), which is v3 §5.1 'the C4 formulas applied to the model episode matched to the real longest episode'. Both variants give the same values.

P2 ties and the P7b start-station test. Report 2 lists both as two-reading, and I agree, so the code's reading stands. Neither can matter on these days: report 2 found 0 tie days, and the real start station was congested on 22/22 days. A stricter reading could only lower these shares.

Test-suite gaps. Report 3 treats them as one-reading deviations, and I agree they fall short of §B10. But no production code changes with them, so no test can 'fail on the code that produced the result' (v5 §B11.2 item 1). checkers.summary:
I went through all 39 findings and 6 critic gaps in freeze_audit_20261011_rows.json, and on the audit's findings the STOP (in-sample screen) cannot be reversed. No item can change J5, and so none can change the nominal: 7192011 (J5 0.2913) remains, ahead of 7192014 (0.3522). No item can change step-halving, which passes with relative changes of 1.1e-5 on J5 and 3.4e-5 on J_v4 and identical day sets. No item can change P11-k (0 unbacked days) or any screen verdict.

**What reversal would need.** 12 screened rows fail. I re-derived all 24 row verdicts from the recorded statistics using the gate's conditions (metanet_gate.py:267-471), and all of them agree with the record. The committed record's screen is identical to freeze_stops.json. A screen-only fix would have to flip all 12 failing rows, and many fail by wide margins: P7b 3/22, P7c 55 min, P7a-1 62.5 min, P1c with median D_N2 of +0.198. Moving the plant would need a fix that changes J5, and no finding alters any J5 item value:
- `s1_ratio` is called only by P9 (metanet_gate.py:446), and P9 is not a J5 row.
- `_variant` runs only inside `sensitivities()`.
- j5-04 concerns only a count that is not reported. The items are still left out of the row mean as the protocol says.
- `loo_nulls`: I checked on the real calibration data that it equals `metanet_gate.nulls()` run on the other 21 days, bit for bit for all 22 days.

**regression-01.** The code does contradict v3 §5.4 on windows of 1-2 bins. It never acts on the calibration days:
- All 22 heavy-first days are B1.
- Real P9 windows are 20-58 bins. On the 6 truncated days, cut − rs is 12-23 bins and the real windows are 24-35 bins.
- The model window is at least min(13, cut − rs − 6) ≥ 6 bins, because the match tolerance is 18 bins (metanet_events.py:94).
- The live `F.day_events` output equals the committed facts on all 22 days.

So the fix gives bit-identical results there. P9 also fails on its count alone (15 matched, 17 needed). The 0-bin path from the tag was not reached either.

**The other one-reading deviations** in production code or record content touch only reports, labels, the record, or the grid and gate stages, which never ran: freeze-05, robustness-03, j5-04, freeze-02, freeze-08 / robustness-06, and critic gaps 2 and 4. The 19 test-gap findings are deviations of the test suite only: in each case the protocol text has one reading and the tests fall short of it. The production code that produced the result is consistent with the text. A test-only fix cannot meet §B11.2's requirement of a test that "fails on the code that produced the result" (v5 line 541), so these are items to disclose, not triggers for a re-run.

**Limits of this sweep:**
- Critic gap 1: the imported modules unchanged since the checkpoint (metanet_events, metanet_inputs, metanet_facts, corridor_analysis, mndot) were not reviewed by any lens. Whether they hold a deviation is not determined.
- A §B11.2 re-run with only these text-match fixes would use an unchanged J5 on the original seeds. It would reproduce the STOP if the run is deterministic, which I did not re-check.
- I did not simulate the nominal; the model-window bound comes from the code, not from a run.
- I did not re-run the reviewers' harnesses (t30b_full, j5_indep, j5_zero). For those I rely on the audit's recorded results.

The repo was not modified, and I read no validation-day data. The scratch scripts are in /tmp/claude-1000/-srv-shared-Workspace-phd-phd-speed-harmo-v5/06097ac8-c9f1-4c3e-b217-abb0461bbd07/scratchpad/v5stopverify/:

deviations.evidence:
Text: v3 §5.4 "S1 = the maximum 3-bin rolling 15-min flow at b's downstream station in [onset − 60 min, end]". A 1- or 2-bin window holds no 3-bin rolling flow under either reading (window fully inside, or rolling value at times inside). Yet metanet_items.py:100 returns seg.sum()/3, reproduced: [300,300,300] for a 1-bin seg of 900. So the code contradicts the text, although the replacement (None) is a choice.

Where it can act: s1_ratio is called only at metanet_gate.py:446, i.e. only P9's S1. It is not used by J5: the facts rows list has no P9, and J5 uses only p4/p5a/p7a/p5c/p7b/p8 items (metanet_j5_eval.py:89-112, metanet_j5.py:82). It is not used by step-halving or P11-k either.

Calibration days (committed facts; live F.day_events equals the facts on 22/22 days, 0 mismatches):
- All 22 days are heavy-first with b = B1.
- Real P9 windows are 20-58 bins.
- 6 days are truncated (20230517, 0531, 0607, 0621, 0920, 1115). Their cut − rs is 16, 23, 20, 14, 13 and 12 bins, giving real windows of 24-35 bins.
- Model window = min(me − ms + 13, cut − ms + 12). Here me ≥ ms and |ms − rs| ≤ 18 (match_episodes tol_bins=18, metanet_events.py:94), so the window is ≥ min(13, cut − rs − 6) ≥ 6 bins.

So the 1-2-bin (and 0-bin) path is never reached, and a fix is bit-identical on calibration days. I did not simulate the nominal; the bound is analytic.

P9 also fails on its count alone (15 < 17, metanet_gate.py:467,471), and 11 other rows fail. Latent for the validation gate only.

Test-33 scope gap against §B10 33 (one reading). The audit's skeptic found no validation read in grid_job, premise or screen by reading. A test cannot change J5, a stop or a screen value. A test-only fix cannot meet v5 line 541.

§B5 "Reported alongside (report-only; cannot change the verdict): ... the excess vehicle-hours ratio (v3 §5.5) and the median in-episode v_u error" is missing from the record. That is a one-reading deviation in report output.

T/2: v4 line 361 says "The v4 record stores T and T/2". Whether it binds the v5 record is a reading question.

By the text itself, neither can change the verdict. Neither enters J5 or any stop.

checkers.summary:
I recomputed P2, P3-1, P4-1, P5a-1 and P7a-1 independently on the 22 calibration days for nominal 7192011. All five match freeze_stops.json exactly, and all five FAIL. I found no deviation in these rows where the committed text has one reading and the code contradicts it. Nothing here can reverse the STOP (in-sample screen).

**What I recomputed.** Each statistic and pass rule comes from the protocol text: v3 §5.1-§5.4, the §5.2 minima at the calibration n, and v5 §B5. Thresholds: P2 ≥ 80 % of n_A; P3-1 ≥ 75 %; P4-1 median ≤ 15 min and ≥ 75 % matched; P5a-1 needs ≥ max(6, ⌈0.75·22⌉) = 17 heavy matched days and |median D| ≤ 0.05; P7a-1 median ≤ 30 min. The calibration counts meet every real-data minimum (n_A,1 = n_H,1 = n_H,first = 22), so all five rows are screened. No pass rule uses a Wilson bound: P2 and P3 are gated on the point share, and their Wilson intervals are reported only.

**Plant run.** I simulated the frozen parameters (equal to C.to_params(nominal_x)) with the committed vsl_lab/plants/metanet.py at T = 0.75 s. The inputs come from C.load_data(); their sha256 matches the facts, and d0/d_o/beta equal the screen's calib_screen_data.npz bit for bit. Clipping max is 0.0077 and no value is non-finite.

**Own code.** The event rule, observation operator, matching, ±60-min overlap, censoring, C4 and every row statistic are my own implementation; no gate/postcal/items/events row function is called. I also rebuilt the real event layer from the raw Mayfly files of the 22 calibration days. It reproduces the committed facts exactly: episodes at every pair, station validity, and the B1 Q_dis and censored durations.

**Recorded vs mine (identical in every case):**
- **P2:** 16/22 = 0.727; needs 18.
- **P3-1:** 16/22 = 0.727; needs 17.
- **P4-1:** 17 of 26 matched (0.654), median 20 min.
- **P5a-1:** 15 matched, 17 required; median D −0.0561.
- **P7a-1:** median 62.5 min. Signed median, uncensored median and all bootstrap CIs (seed 7,192,099) also match.

**Why the margins cannot close.** On 5 of the 6 miss days the model has no P_1 episode at all. On 20230607 its only P_1 episode starts 100 min after the real one ends. The P5a-1 count shortfall fails the row on its own, and P7a-1 is more than 2 × its threshold.

**Alternative readings tested, model and real side alike.** None changes a verdict:
- the merge-gap measure (only P7a-1 moves, to 67.5);
- overlap ±55 and ±65 min;
- match window ±95 min;
- unmasked model flow;
- matching the longest real episode alone;
- the t_c window at e + 7 bins;
- the order of tied matches.

The candidate items listed are ambiguities or a report-only CI; none could change the route.

**Could any difference turn the screen into a PASS?** No. None was found, and each of the five rows fails the screen by itself. Seven further rows also failed in the record (P1c, P5b-1, P6-1, P5c, P7b, P7c, P9); I did not recompute them.

**Limits.** I did not independently verify the plant, the replay input arrays or the c_s table; I used them as committed. I extracted the c_s table by decoding only the 'c_s' object at its byte offset in precal_part1.json. The file was read into memory, but no other part was decoded or shown.

**Validation data.** None was opened: no val_data.npz, no validation-date raw files, no F11 field.

**Repo.** Read-only; no edit, commit or git state change.

**What I checked.** I read v5 §B5 (lines 350-375) and the texts it points to: v3 §5.1-§5.4 (lines 824-1007), v3 R4(b), F8, v4 §A1/§A12 and the v4 addendum. **What the code does, row by row against §B5.**
- Real-data minima (v3:849-852): all are met at n = 22. n_A,1 = 22 and n_A,2 = 9 (≥ 8); n_H,1 = 22 and n_H,2 = 9 (≥ 6); n_H,first = 22. So no row is "reported, not screened", and P5c is gated (n_H,both = 9 ≥ 6).

- Thresholds are point statistics except P1c-vs-N1, which uses the upper bound of a 10,000-resample percentile bootstrap (seed 7,192,099). Wilson intervals are reported only, as the text says.
- P5b(ii) uses F8 B1 ci_r[0] = 0.99397, computed over 22 heavy days, as §B5 requires.
- P6-1: the real gradient is 0, so (b)-(c) are not applied, as the text requires.
- P1c: the nulls leave the scored day out; N1 is the median of speeds ≥ 45 mph and N2 the per-bin median, on scaled speeds.
- P7b and P7c follow v3 §5.4.

**Rows that fail on their own statistics.** None of these is touched by any deviation:
- P1c: median D_N1 = +0.107, median D_N2 = +0.198.

- P5c's denominator is n_real_merge_defined instead of n_H,both. Both equal 9 here, and a correction would only make the row stricter.
- s1_ratio mishandles windows of 1-2 bins (audit regression-01). No window here is shorter than 20 bins, and P9 fails on its count anyway.
- Two two-reading points, so the code's reading stands: P2 ties (none occurred) and P7b not testing the start station for congestion (the real start was congested on every day).
- Missing report-only items, which §B5 says cannot change the verdict.
- Missing tests 34 and 31 (test gaps only).

rows.note: n_H,both = 9 ≥ 6, so the row is gated and screened. need(9) = 7, and only 4 days are heavy-matched at both, so it fails on the model-side minimum, which the text (one reading) makes a FAIL. |median D| = 0.038 would pass. The code's denominator is n_real_merge_defined rather than n_H,both. Both are 9 here, and the correction could only raise the requirement.

rows.code_ref: vsl_lab/jobs/metanet_gate.py:127-152 (congested, extent), 390-401; metanet_items.py:53-75 (start station, matched windows, hit = err ≤ 1 in the real-valid order)
rows.protocol_quote: v3:956-960 'Start station: real side, the upstream station of the most upstream bottleneck with a real episode ... Model side, the same for ... a model episode matched to a real episode'; 'Congested station: event-layer speed < 40 mph for ≥ 15 consecutive minutes overlapping the window'; v3:904 'model extent = the real extent station or an adjacent speed-valid station on ≥ 70 % of the days'
rows.note: 3 of 22 hits (0816, 0830, 0920). The reproduction shows the mechanism. Real extents are S1771–S1773. The model's B1 queue spills to S459, S460, S461 or S453 (err 3–11 stations), and 3 days have no matched model episode. Units are consistent (both sides in mph, metanet_events.py:53). The start station not being tested for congestion is a two-reading point. The real start station was congested on 22/22 days, and a stricter reading could only remove hits.

rows.protocol_quote: v3:963-964 'Real union interval: merge the day's real P_1 and P_2 episodes ... with the < 30-min gap rule ... dur_sys,model = the length of the longest model union interval that overlaps (±60 min) the real one, or 0 if none overlaps'; v3:905 'median ≤ 30 min'
rows.note: The median is 55 min. I recomputed it from the reproduced per-day values (5 to 230 min). The construction (all model P_1 and P_2 episodes, gap < 6 empty bins, ±12-bin overlap, 0 if none) matches the text.

rows.protocol_quote: v3:883 'P9 needs heavy matched first-active days ≥ max(6, ⌈0.75 · n_H,first⌉), and P9(2) needs ≥ 5 days with model excess'; v3:880 'a model-dependent shortfall is a FAIL'; v5:359 'P9 reads its replayed exit flows from metanet_v5/calib_screen_data.npz'
rows.note: n_H,first = 22 ≥ 6, so the row is screened. need = 17 and only 15 days are matched, so it fails on the count alone. The statistics would pass: S1 diff −0.006 ≤ +0.03, and S2 1.5 ≥ 1.2 on 15 days (5 needed). The s1_ratio defect for windows of 1–2 bins (audit regression-01) does not apply here: the shortest windows are 20 bins (real) and 23 (model). It cannot change the count in any case.

deviations.evidence: metanet_gate.py:379 and 387-388 use need(len(both_q)), where both_q = days heavy at both with the real merge section defined. v3:884 says '≥ max(6, ⌈0.75 · n_H,both⌉)'. The recorded row has n_H_both = 9 = n_real_merge_defined, so the requirement is 7 either way. Correcting it can only raise the requirement, never turn the FAIL (4 < 7) into a PASS. Caveat: one could argue the text does not cover days without a real merge value, so 'one reading' is my judgement.

metanet_items.py:96-101: np.convolve 'valid' on a window of 1–2 bins returns seg.sum()/3, against v3 §5.4 'the maximum 3-bin rolling 15-min flow ... in [onset − 60 min, end]'. In the reproduction the shortest P9 window is 20 bins (real) and 23 (model), so no value changes. P9 fails on its count (15 < 17), which s1_ratio does not touch.

metanet_gate.py:310 passes a day if e*'s pair is among several model episodes tied at the earliest onset. v3:947 'the one with the earliest onset must be at e*'s pair' does not settle ties, so the code's reading stands (§B11.2). The reproduction found 0 tie days, and a stricter reading could only lower the share.

metanet_gate.py:144 sets the extent to the start station before walking upstream, without testing that the start station is congested. v3:959 'the unbroken run of congested stations that starts at the start station' admits both readings. The real start station was congested on 22/22 days in the reproduction. A stricter reading could only turn hits into misses, and P7b is 3/22.

v5:375 requires 'the excess vehicle-hours ratio (v3 §5.5) and the median in-episode v_u error'. They are absent from screen() (metanet_v5_freeze.py:153-194) and from the record. §B5 labels them 'report-only; cannot change the verdict'.

v5 §B10 test 34 requires that the screen 'returns STOP for a synthetic failing plant', and test 31 that 'the P1c nulls leave out day d'. No test calls screen() with a failing or below-minimum row, or tests loo_nulls. These are test gaps and change no number. My reproduction of the real screen gave every row identical (to 1e-12) to freeze_stops.json.
